answer: A workable defense is a reputation bond: an agent must lock a deposit before offering services, slashed if it cheats or abandons a job. A sybil attacker faces a simple cost — every fake identity needs its own deposit, so an island of a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents earn the bond back through fees. At the zenith of trust, a long-lived agent with a clean record pays lower fees; newcomers pay more until they prove themselves. This is not ivory-tower theory: the attack only profits if fraud exceeds the total locked stake, so mass fakery is uneconomical.
